title: What does the proposed Pax Silica bill in the House contain?
summary: A House bill in the early stages seeks to provide the framework on how to manage the planned semiconductor hub

blocks.text: Graphics by Nico Villarete/Rappler
A House bill in the early stages seeks to provide the framework on how to manage the planned semiconductor hub

items: During President Trump's visit to the Philippines, no Pax Silica agreement was signed, but House lawmakers are proposing legislation to support an AI-native industrial hub in New Clark City.

House Bill No. 11758 aims to establish an Advanced Industries Zone and the Advanced Industries Development Authority (AIDA), which would oversee operations and provide incentives for qualified enterprises in high-tech industries.

When US President Donald Trump visited the Philippines during the ASEAN Summit, he signed no Pax Silica agreement with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

But even as major hurdles hound a possible deal, administration-allied House lawmakers are ready to supplement a Pax Silica initiative with a bill clearing the bureaucratic and legal obstacles to an AI-native industrial acceleration hub in New Clark City in Capas, Tarlac.
House Bill No. 11758, filed in October by six congressmen led by Deputy Speaker Ronnie Puno, is called the Advanced Industries Development Act.
The bill seeks to create an Advanced Industries Zone, as well as its independent government body called the Advanced Industries Development Authority (AIDA).
The Zone is envisaged to be “decentralized, self-reliant, and self-sustaining…with minimum government intervention.”
The AIDA, meanwhile, would be run by a board, composed of 11 governors, including a chairperson appointed by the President.

Based on the proposal, the AIDA would be tasked to administer the Zone and oversee persons and entities with projects in it. They would fix and collect fees, enter into contracts, and have an authorized capital of P50 billion.
If it becomes law, the AIDA would effectively be given a 25-year, renewable, franchise “to construct, operate, and maintain systems for power and water distribution within the Zone.”

Under the proposal, a person or an entity (called a locator) can apply for certification as a qualified enterprise with AIDA’s board of governors. This would allow them to do business within the Zone.
But to be a qualified enterprise, they must meet the minimum investment capital worth P15 billion, excluding land value.
Their enterprise must belong to any of the following high-tech industries:

items: semiconductor design, fabrication, assembly, testing, or packaging
advanced manufacturing (automation, robotics, precision engineering, or advanced materials)
data centers and computing infrastructure for AI computing
processing of critical minerals and specialty materials
scientific research, development, and technology commercialization

blocks.text: Marcos previously said the Philippine development under the Pax Silica initiative would include the construction of data centers, an issue that is at the heart of environmental groups’ opposition.
Based on the proposal, qualified enterprises would enjoy exclusive financial incentives and operational privileges for their projects within the zone. These include:

items: income tax holiday for seven years from the start of project’s commercial operations
special corporate income tax or enhanced deductions regime in lieu of or upon the expiration of the income tax holiday
exemptions from value-added tax and customs duty

blocks.text: The Pax Silica initiative has been met with intense pushback in the Philippines amid fears that hundreds of indigenous peoples and farmers in Tarlac province would be displaced.
The House bill explicitly excludes ancestral lands from being declared alienable and disposable.

Human Rights Watch said Aeta comunities in Capas have been seeking recognition of their ancestral domain since the 1990s, but have yet to receive the title. The IPs have been informed by the government that their homes and land would be affected by the Pax Silica project, and that they would be relocated by December.

The House bill gives preferential hiring to Capas residents, members of IP communities whose ancestral domains are within or adjacent to the Zone, and potentially displaced persons due to the project.

blocks.text: HB 11758, whose other authors include congressmen Miguel Luis Villafuerte, Albert Garcia, Alfredo Maranon III, Rolando Valeriano, and Jolo Revilla, is in the early stages of the legislative process.
It has been referred to the economic affairs committee, but has yet to be tackled.

As with many bills, this proposal could gain further traction if backed by the House leadership — or if House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos or House Speaker Bojie Dy files their own version of the measure.
So far, the bill is not yet a Palace priority measure, and has no counterpart in the Senate. – Rappler.com
